topic: Allahabad HC: grandparents' better financial resources alone are no ground to take a minor child's custody away from his mother - special appeal against Single Judge's habeas corpus order (27 May 2026) dismissed; Single Judge weighed tender age, continuity of care, emotional bond, schooling and Section 6, Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956; grandparents may help financially and seek visitation before the district court (Manoj Sahlot & Another v. State of U.P. & 6 Others, 2026 LiveLaw (AB) 941, Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and Justice Kshitij Shailendra, reported 15 Nov 2026)

slides.title: More money does not mean **more right** to the child
slides.subtitle: Grandparents being richer is **not a reason** to take a child away from his mother, says the Allahabad High Court.
slides.cite: **Manoj Sahlot & Another v. State of U.P. & 6 Others** · 2026 LiveLaw (AB) 941 · Allahabad High Court · Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and Justice Kshitij Shailendra · reported 15 November 2026

slides.label: What happened
slides.title: A son kept away from **his mother**
bullets: After her husband's death in November 2025, a mother went to his family home with her parents and her **two children**.
She says the paternal grandparents **kept her 8-year-old son** after the cremation. Her 4-year-old daughter stayed with her.
Police did not help, so she filed a **habeas corpus** petition. On 27 May 2026, a Single Judge gave **custody to the mother**.

slides.label: The appeal
slides.title: The grandparents' **argument**
bullets: The grandparents appealed. They said they were **financially better off**, and the mother's income of about **Rs 20,000 a month** from tuition was not enough.
They claimed custody was given to her **only because she is the mother**.
They also objected that they had been **denied visitation**.

slides.label: What the Court held
slides.title: Welfare, not **wealth**
bullets: Better finances, **by themselves**, cannot be a ground to deprive a mother of her minor son's custody.
The Single Judge had weighed the child's **tender age, continuity of care, emotional bond, schooling** and Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956.
The Bench called it a **well-structured order** and dismissed the appeal. The boy had also been separated from his **younger sister**.

slides.label: What it means for you
slides.title: Money can **help**, not decide
bullets: The Court said the grandparents could **give financial support** for the children's upbringing instead of seeking custody.
For visitation, they can approach the **district court** or start fresh proceedings.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.
slides.note: Keep in mind: this does not mean a mother always gets custody. Courts look at the child's overall welfare in each case.

caption:
Being richer does not give grandparents a better claim to a child than his mother 👩‍👦⚖️

The Allahabad High Court has dismissed an appeal by a boy's paternal grandparents who wanted to keep him away from his mother. After her husband's death in November 2025, the mother says the grandparents kept her 8-year-old son with them, while her 4-year-old daughter stayed with her. When the police did not help, she filed a habeas corpus petition, and on 27 May 2026 a Single Judge handed custody of the boy to her.

In appeal, the grandparents argued that they had more money, that the mother earned only about Rs 20,000 a month from tuition, and that she got custody just because she is the mother. The Division Bench disagreed. It said better financial resources, on their own, cannot be a reason to take a minor son away from his mother. The Single Judge had looked at the child's tender age, continuity of care, emotional bond, schooling and Section 6 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, and the Bench found it a well-structured order.

The Court suggested that the grandparents could support the children financially instead of seeking custody. On visitation, it left them free to approach the district court or start fresh proceedings. Remember, custody is always decided on the child's welfare in each case.

Case: Manoj Sahlot & Another v. State of U.P. & 6 Others, 2026 LiveLaw (AB) 941
Court: Allahabad High Court, Chief Justice Arun Bhansali and Justice Kshitij Shailendra, reported 15 November 2026
